focus: Unread releases for hooks and plugins: v4.0.0.3 live-sync on Cursor/Devin plus the hook list's why-not notes, v4.0.0.13 17-plugin dual-compat claim with the shared shim and the plugin test run, and injection-contract.md against today's adapters.

label: At HEAD the OpenCode plugin suite is red: node --test .opencode/plugins/tests/*.test.cjs reports 572 tests, 545 pass, 27 fail, 0 skipped, and every failure sits in the session-relaunch nudge path. The shared helper startLoopNudge asserts transform() returns one nudge entry at 90 percent fill and gets 0, so four dependent cases then die on undefined.match. v4.0.0.13 claims 533 plugin tests passing and three automated checks in CI, so either this suite is not gated or a post-4.0.0.13 opencode commit regressed it.

v4.0.0.13 says all 17 plugins run on OpenCode 2 and 1, sixteen through the shared adapter and sk-vision on its own. The tree now holds 19 plugin modules in .opencode/plugins and all 19 import dualPlugin, and sk-vision was deleted outright, so the one plugin that is supposed to bypass the shim has no referent and a reader auditing the shim cannot use the note to find its exception.

injection-contract.md states session relaunch ships off and that SYSTEM_SESSION_RELAUNCH_ENABLED decides otherwise, while the live hook-flags.env sets SYSTEM_SESSION_RELAUNCH_ENABLED=1 and pins only Claude to 0, which leaves OpenCode, Pi, Codex and Hermes enabled by inheritance. Either the doc describes the example file rather than the shipped repo or the live file contradicts it; whether hook-flags.env is tracked was not established this iteration, so authority between the two is undetermined.

v4.0.0.3's hook-coverage claim holds on inspection: git-live-follow runs from both .cursor/hooks.json and .devin/hooks.v1.json, and the hook list names the tools that cannot carry the injection screen and why. Focus item 1 closed with no drift.

A plugin-inventory.json and plugin-inventory.test.cjs already exist under .opencode/plugins/tests, so a machine-readable plugin count is available and was not read this iteration; f-iter009-002's count came from a directory listing.

direction: Read f-iter009-001 as an environment-only mtime flake
reason: Three flags-file tests do read like timestamp-granularity flakes, but the 24 remaining failures share one startLoopNudge assertion returning 0 entries, which is not a clock artifact. Splitting the run per file would settle which half is environmental.
